name: u-boot-tools
why: Tools like mkimage and dumpimage open up bootloader images, a real door into firmware, though fairly niche.

brief.what_it_is: The u-boot-tools Homebrew formula installs three host-side utilities (dumpimage, mkenvimage, mkimage) from the U-Boot project. U-Boot itself is a free, open-source boot loader for many architectures (ARM, MIPS, PowerPC, RISC-V, x86, x86_64) that initializes hardware and then boots the device's OS kernel. The homepage does not describe these three tools specifically, and the docs I read do not show their inputs or outputs. The docs only explain how to build the host tools from the U-Boot source tree.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames U-Boot as a boot loader whose purpose is to perform various hardware initialization tasks and boot the device's operating system kernel. The docs say the tools-only build exists so distributions can ship all possible tools in a generic way, without building specific tools for each machine.
brief.how_it_works: The docs describe a tools-only defconfig that builds the host utilities from the U-Boot source tree on Linux, with a separate route for Windows through MSYS2. On Windows it needs gcc, make, bison, diffutils and openssl-devel. By default the tools-only build also builds pylibfdt, and NO_PYTHON=1 turns that off. I did not read the mkimage, dumpimage or mkenvimage pages, so I cannot describe their internal workings.

brief.install_notes: The brew formula is a packaging of the U-Boot host tools, so I did not see a separate install procedure for it. Building from source needs a U-Boot source checkout and make. Windows builds use MSYS2 with gcc, make, bison, diffutils and openssl-devel. The pylibfdt Python binding is built by default unless NO_PYTHON=1 is set.
brief.standout: This is a niche, fairly unusual part of firmware tooling: small command-line utilities that work on U-Boot's own image formats. The docs say the tools are built from the same source tree as the boot loader, so they are tied to a specific U-Boot release.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists v2026.10 as the latest stable release, dated 06 July 2026, and the project has a mailing list, IRC channel and custodian trees. I did not check the Homebrew formula's own update history.
brief.caveats: The homepage and docs describe U-Boot the boot loader, not the three binaries, so I could not confirm what mkimage, dumpimage or mkenvimage take in or produce. I saw no usage examples for them. The docs are described as a work in progress. Windows builds need MSYS2 and several specific package versions. The brew formula's caveats field is empty. The scout note calls the tools a 'real door into firmware', but I did not verify that claim from the pages I read.

entry.title: u-boot-tools
entry.tldr: Host-side utilities from the U-Boot boot loader project, for working with the image and environment files that small devices boot from.
entry.deeper_look:
U-Boot is a free, open-source boot loader used on many architectures, including ARM, MIPS, PowerPC, RISC-V and x86. It runs first on a device, initializes hardware, then hands off to the operating system kernel. This formula installs three of its host-side utilities, `mkimage`, `dumpimage` and `mkenvimage`, so they run on your own machine instead of on the device.

The docs describe these tools as a separate tools-only build from the U-Boot source tree. The stated reason is that distributions can ship all the possible tools in a generic way, without building specific tools for each machine. The project's docs I read did not describe what each of the three tools takes in or produces, so this entry does not either. By name, they deal with boot images and environment files.

The idea underneath is that a device's boot process is made of files that something has to build and package. Learning to read and make those files is a way into how firmware gets from storage to a running kernel. The tools are built from the same source tree as the boot loader, so they are tied to a specific U-Boot release.

entry.whats_unique: These are small command-line utilities for U-Boot's own image formats, a niche corner of firmware tooling that most developers never see.
entry.caveats: The docs I read cover building the tools, not using them, and describe themselves as a work in progress, so expect to learn usage from the --help output; real use also assumes you have a board or image to work on.
